items.title: 61426_Jacques Butler oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee narrates a story about Sidney Bechet and Gene Brouillard interacting in a court setting, but does not describe a personal relationship between himself and Brouillard.

ctx.x: So, "I say again, let the guillotine do its duty for things of this nature." Bechet started crying and moaning back, and went into convulsions. and got on the floor and wallowed on his /The judge says, "Arrete! Arrete!" "Get him un from there!" So they got Bechet back in there, helped him (inaudible). And the judge was whispering -- see there are three judges, you know, sometimes four. And they began to whisper to this main judge. The main judge pointed at Bechet and Bechet went into his act again.

So Gene Brouillard was sitting in the court and the judge looked at Bechet and he's about to bow his head. I think I'd better do something to him. So he and Brouillard come up immediately. He says, "Judge," and he had all these medals on him, all from when he was in the Foreign Legion, Croix de Guerre, Legion de Honor (inaudible).

"May I have a word?" And the lawyer for Mike McKenzie, his name was Torez, a great lawyer, one of those type of lawyers at that time. So he said, from what bar are you? And Gene Brouillard says, "I'm from the bar of justice," fraternite, egalite." They have justices -- you know, in all courts you have the main judge (inaudible).
